Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase. South African players are out there in the middle. Netherlands openers Max O'Dowd and Stephan Myburgh are taking guard and we are all set to begin!
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then! 278 needed for Netherlands to win this match. The conditions are overcast but we hope rain stays away from the action. The wicket is batting friendly and someone has to anchor the innings to get near the target. Will they be able to do it? We will find out. Stay tuned as the chase is around the corner.

Roelof van der Merwe is up for a quick chat, he says that it was an enjoyable fifty overs. Says that they created pressure on them in the middle overs and he is happy with the result. Adds that it gets better to bat as the game progresses and they need a good start. Tells that there should not be scoreboard pressure and hopes to build a partnership

Netherlands bowlers were brilliant in their opening spell and Fred Klaassen sent both the South African openers cheaply. There was a good partnership in between but just when South Africa were looking to cut loose Brandon Glover got the key wicket of Zubayr Hamza. Timm van der Gugten got the important wicket of dangerous David Miller and Netherlands bowlers seized the opportunity. They kept chipping in with wickets and had South Africa in all sorts of trouble. Their bowlers missed the mark at the death as the bowlers were carted all around the park by Andile Phehlukwayo in the end. Overall a decent bowling performance and a good start with a bat will make things easy for Netherlands.

South Africa started on a negative note as both their openers departed early. The debutant, Zubayr Hamza and young, Kyle Verreynne got together at the score of 24 and stitched together a brilliant partnership of 119 runs. Both of the batters got to their fifty and both look set for much more. But Hamza departed in the 29th over and that gave Netherlands a chance to get back into the game. There was a brief partnership between Miller and Verreynne but once Miller departed, wickets started crumbling and from 179-3 South Africa went to 209-7 that included the wicket of set batter Kyle Verreynne on 95. In the end, Maharaj and Phehlukwayo got together and took South Africa past 270 as Phehlukwayo played a brilliant cameo of 48 from 22 balls.

86 coming off the last ten overs. Thanks to some incredible hitting from Andile Phehlukwayo and Keshav Maharaj. They will surely be happy with this score going into the break. Apart from the one big partnership in between South African innings never got going as Netherlands bowlers kept chipping in with wickets. But a good 9th wicket partnership at the back end of the innings have taken them to a relatively safer position. It generally gets easy to chase here at Centurion and Netherlands will believe that they are in with a fair chance here.

TOSS - Up goes the coin and it lands in the favour of NETHERLANDS. They have elected to BOWL first.

Netherlands, on the other hand, are also quite an experienced unit. The presence of players like Roelof van der Merwe, Colin Ackermann and a few others with experience of playing in South African conditions makes them quite a formidable side. They have some proven performers like Max O'Dowd and Pieter Seelaar and bowlers like Fred Klaassen and Viv Kingma are more than capable to make use of any help on offer from the deck. Overall, Netherlands definitely has the firepower and experience to challenge Proteas but the hosts iwill still be the favourites going into this game. Will they live up to this favourite tag? We shall find out soon. Stay tuned for the toss and other updates,

South Africa are without their skipper Temba Bavuma and plenty of their other star players but they still have a good mix of experience and youth in their squad. The batting looks strong with Janneman Malan and Reeza Hendricks at the top of the order and David Miller in the middle. While their spin bowling stocks consist of Tabraiz Shamsi and the captain for this series, Keshav Maharaj. The seam bowling looks a little short of experience but the presence of seam bowling allrounders like Dwaine Pretorius, Andile Phehlukwayo makes them quite a balanced unit. Wayne Parnell is making a national comeback after four years and his presence will boost the attack further.

Hello and welcome to the first ODI between South Africa and the Netherlands. The crucial World Cup Super League points are up for grabs and both these teams will be looking to extract as many points from this series as possible. South Africa are currently ranked 9th on that table and going by their present rank, they are not among the sides to qualify directly for the 2023 World Cup. But things could change quite quickly and they can climb to the number 3 spot if they beat Netherlands in all three ODIs. But Netherlands are no pushovers and have plenty of experience and quality on their side. Netherlands will also be looking to climb up the ladder on that points table and will be eager to prove a point by beating a full member at their home. Will they challenge Proteas? Or will South Africa dominate?
